guard: an isolated legacy manager owns a PTY that ends when the manager dies and exposes no durable runtime reference
why: The fixture creates the real current PtyRuntime in one isolated Node process, records the actual manager and counter child pids, then kills only the manager it created. It distinguishes a live process from a zombie through /proc before reporting the red condition.

Both mutation windows are code-only. The first removes the absence of a durable reference. The second suppresses the manager-death outcome. The named cells prove the fixture is not merely checking a child it never owned.

mutations.name: M1 make the legacy PTY claim a durable reference
mutations.expectRed: legacy PTY exposes no durable reference a successor can adopt
mutations.cell: legacy PTY exposes no durable reference a successor can adopt
mutations.note: The fixture reads the handle the real current PtyRuntime returned. Reversing this code-only boolean makes the test observe a reference where legacy custody must expose none.

mutations.name: M2 suppress the manager-owned PTY death observation
mutations.expectRed: M1 red: legacy manager death ends the manager-owned counter PTY
mutations.cell: M1 red: legacy manager death ends the manager-owned counter PTY
mutations.note: The mutation is only the final child-death predicate. The earlier cells still arm the fixture, establish the child live, and prove the actual manager died before this named cell reddens.
